title: High‐Entropy Oxides for Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Structural Design, Reaction Mechanisms, and Future Perspectives
content:
High‐entropy oxides provide diverse local environments for tailoring oxygen evolution catalysis. This review connects synthesis strategies and crystal structures with multielement interactions and reaction mechanisms, highlighting Ir/Ru‐based rutile oxides for acidic water electrolysis. Insights into catalytic activity, structural stability, and noble‐metal utilization inform catalyst design and translation toward proton‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzers.








ABSTRACT
The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a kinetically demanding anodic process in water electrolysis and related electrochemical energy‐conversion systems. Its multistep proton‐coupled electron‐transfer kinetics and catalyst degradation under strongly oxidizing conditions limit overall efficiency and durability. High‐entropy oxides (HEOs), which combine multicomponent configurational disorder, lattice distortion, broad distributions of local coordination environments, and element‐specific electronic interactions, have emerged as a versatile platform for OER catalyst design. This review summarizes the definitions and physicochemical characteristics of HEOs, OER reaction pathways, theoretical and data‐driven methods, synthesis strategies, representative crystal structures, and recent progress in acidic OER and proton‐exchange‐membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). Particular attention is given to rutile‐type Ir/Ru‐based HEOs, including their phase formation, local electronic‐structure regulation, degradation behavior, and device‐level validation. Current challenges in composition‐space exploration, operando mechanism identification, long‐term stability, noble‐metal utilization, reproducible scale‐up, and standardized device testing are discussed, together with directions for future research.

title: Advances in Bio‐Integrated Edge Computing Systems for Smart and Connected Health
content:
This review explores advances in bio‐integrated edge computing for healthcare, focusing on co‐designing computing, sensing, and energy strategies to overcome integration and power challenges for optimized, decentralized operation.








ABSTRACT
Recent advances in bio‐integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high‐resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low‐latency, energy‐efficient, and privacy‐preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio‐integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co‐design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute‐in‐memory and neuromorphic systems, for on‐device data processing and decision‐making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.

title: Toward Scalable Applications of Biomass Aerogels for Building Thermal Insulation
content:
An application‐driven structure–failure–qualification framework connects retained composition, product formats, pore and interfacial architectures, building envelope functions, service‐induced failure, and validation pathways. By distinguishing laboratory performance from product evidence, it shifts biomass aerogel research from isolated property records toward scalable, application‐specific insulation products defined by thermal performance, durability, reaction‐to‐fire behavior, manufacturability, and qualification.








ABSTRACT
Biomass aerogels are emerging as lightweight porous materials for building envelope insulation. Reported thermal conductivities span approximately 13 to 170 mW m−1 K−1 and densities 8–260 kg m−3 across diverse feedstocks, pore architectures, and hybrid formulations. Translation into building products remains constrained by structural instability, moisture‐induced property loss, formulation‐dependent fire behavior, interfacial degradation, energy‐intensive processing, and limited product‐level validation. We introduce an application‐driven structure–failure–qualification framework linking feedstock compositions and product formats to building‐specific performance requirements, pore structure designs, dominant service‐induced failure modes, and validation requirements. We compare major biomass and hybrid material classes, product formats, and pore architectures according to their performance trade‐offs, service vulnerability, and maturity of evidence. Multiscale pore engineering and bioinspired architectures can reconcile thermal insulation with mechanical integrity and environmental stability, but favorable specimen‐scale properties do not necessarily establish deployment readiness. By connecting structure–property relationships with service condition reliability and standardised benchmarks, we elucidate the requirements for real‐world translation. Future progress will require scalable hierarchical design, long‐term durability validation, and harmonised sustainability assessment to support integration into next‐generation low‐carbon buildings.

title: Piezocatalysis: Concepts, Advances, and Opportunities
content:
Piezocatalysis converts mechanical excitation into polarization‐driven charge separation and surface redox chemistry. This review unifies energy‐band theory, screening effects, piezoelectric materials, reaction mechanisms, performance‐enhancement strategies, and applications in environmental remediation, energy conversion, chemical synthesis, and biomedicine. Remaining challenges and emerging opportunities are critically assessed to guide reliable benchmarking and practical development.








ABSTRACT
Piezocatalysis has recently emerged as a distinct paradigm of force‐driven catalysis, in which mechanical stress applied to piezoelectric materials induces internal electric fields that activate redox reactions under mild conditions. This mechanical‐to‐electrical energy conversion offers a new catalytic activation mode, particularly suited for scenarios where conventional stimuli are unavailable or undesirable. Over the past decade, substantial progress has been achieved in elucidating fundamental mechanisms, advancing material platforms, and demonstrating functional applications spanning environmental remediation, sustainable energy conversion, and biomedical therapies. Despite these advances, the field still lacks an integrated framework that connects fundamental concepts, mechanistic models, material design, performance optimization, standardized evaluation and benchmarking, and practical applications. This review establishes such a framework by systematically integrating these elements into a coherent structure for understanding, evaluating, and advancing piezocatalysis. Throughout, we place particular emphasis on what evidence is required to identify genuine piezocatalysis, how catalytic performance should be benchmarked under different mechanical inputs, and how conventional piezoelectric parameters relate to catalytic activity. We further discuss representative applications and outline remaining challenges and future opportunities, aiming to advance piezocatalysis from laboratory demonstrations toward reliable, efficient, and practical catalytic processes.

title: A Quasi‐n‐i‐p Architecture Realized by Sequential Lamination Delivers 20.58% Efficiency in Inverted Organic Solar Cells
content:
Sequential lamination constructs an acceptor‐rich/bulk‐heterojunction/donor‐rich quasi‐n‐i‐p active‐layer architecture in inverted organic solar cells, creating a favorable vertical composition gradient across the active layer. This graded architecture facilitates charge extraction, balances carrier transport, and suppresses recombination, thereby enabling a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.58% and highlighting the effectiveness of sequential lamination for high‐performance inverted devices.








ABSTRACT
Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal‐oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi‐n‐i‐p active layer comprising an acceptor‐rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor‐rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes cascade energy‐level alignment and preserves interfacial integrity, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction and suppressing recombination losses. As a result, the optimal device achieves a PCE of 20.58%, with a certified efficiency of 20.07%, placing it among the highest reported for single‐junction inverted OSCs. This architecture was successfully fabricated with different donor‐rich layers, BHJ cores, and acceptor‐rich layers, demonstrating broader material applicability across multiple material combinations. Interfacial adhesion and vertical compositional control improve electrical continuity, enhance charge generation and transport, and reduce trap‐assisted and bimolecular recombination, leading to higher open‐circuit voltage, short‐circuit current density, and fill factor. This work provides a scalable route to active‐layer engineering in inverted OSCs and offers a general strategy for high‐performance organic photovoltaic fabrication.

title: Biodegradable Capacitive‐Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
content:
Biodegradable capacitive‐coupling bioelectronics (CCB) enables wireless electrical stimulation and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring for peripheral nerve repair. By integrating biodegradable electrodes, an electroactive nerve guidance conduit, and Mo‐wire interconnects, the system promotes coordinated neurovascular regeneration, remyelination, and axon regrowth while dynamically tracking nerve recovery in vivo.








ABSTRACT
Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive‐coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo‐wire interconnects, and a textile‐reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio‐NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery‐free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB‐mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro‐regenerative immune modulation, calcium‐related signaling, AMPK‐associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB‐enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic‐monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

title: Bridging Biosensing and Hardware‐Level Data Security With a Conjugated Radical Polymer
content:
A conjugated radical polymer provides two complementary functions within a common material platform: sensitive dopamine biosensing and device‐specific stochastic electrical responses for security. The work demonstrates a materials‐based approach for combining bioelectronic signal acquisition with hardware‐level authentication while maintaining the distinct operation of the two functions.








ABSTRACT
The integration of biological signal processing with hardware‐level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox‐mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical‐containing backbone. By establishing a material‐level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.

title: Photonic Klein Tunnelling in Silicon Topological Materials for Terahertz 6G Interconnects
content:
Klein tunnelling, the perfect transmission of relativistic particles through potential barriers, is realized optically in a CMOS‐compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. Valley kink states cross engineered inversion‐symmetric barriers with near‐unity transmission, surviving multibarrier cascades, sharp bends and splitters, and carrying error‐free data beyond 100 Gbit/s toward robust 6G photonic interconnects.








ABSTRACT
Topological photonics enables robust light transport along engineered interfaces, but transport across a potential barrier placed within such an interface, and the range of barrier strengths over which it survives, remain largely unexplored. Here we experimentally demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling in a Complementary Metal‐Oxide‐Semiconductor (CMOS) compatible silicon valley photonic crystal at terahertz frequencies. A local, inversion‐symmetric barrier is introduced into a valley kink channel, with its strength Δ controlled through the geometry of the triangular holes. The barrier strength is calibrated using the local Dirac‐frequency shift, establishing a direct relation between photonic crystal geometry and the effective tight‐binding potential. We find that transmission remains close to its barrier‐free value for Δ below the nearest‐neighbour hopping amplitude t, and is strongly suppressed as Δ approaches t. Momentum‐space analysis shows valley pseudospin preserved to better than 98% across two cascaded barriers. We further demonstrate Klein‐tunnelling transport through multibarrier, Ω‐shaped and power‐splitter devices, supporting terahertz data transmission at rates up to 100 Gbit s−1. Our findings underpin a new design framework for resilient and high‐capacity terahertz photonic integrated circuits.

title: Polymer‐Immobilized Organic Salt Anions Enable Enhanced Anode Kinetics and Interfacial Stability in Sodium‐Ion Capacitors
content:
Polymer‐Immobilized Organic Salt Anions represent a regulatory strategy that modulates the local Na+ solvation structure, accelerates interfacial ion transport at the anode, and is compatible with the dual‐ion migration mechanism of SICs. This work establishes an electrolyte‐centric strategy for enhancing the kinetic performance and cycling stability of sodium‐ion capacitors.








ABSTRACT
Sodium‐ion capacitors (SICs) are energy storage devices capable of simultaneously achieving high power density and high energy density. However, due to differences in the kinetics of the anode and cathode, conventional liquid electrolytes struggle to maintain cycling stability and are prone to leakage. To address these issues, herein, we designed a gel polymer electrolyte (GPE) by in situ polymerizing the functional organic salt sodium 2‐acrylamido‐2‐methylpropanesulfonate (AMPSNa) with the crosslinking agent Pentaerythritol triacrylate (PETA). This approach achieves dual transport regulation of anode kinetics by anchoring anions to optimize both Na+ desolvation kinetics and SEI stability. Upon dissociation, AMPSNa anchors the AMPS− ion to the polymer backbone, weakening Na+ solvent interactions. This modifies the Na+ coordination environment and facilitates interfacial transport. Concurrently, the reduction of AMPS− generates inorganic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) components forming a stable, highly ion‐conductive interfacial layer that accelerates Na+ transport. The AC||HC SIC assembled using the GPE‐AMPSNa electrolyte achieved a maximum energy density of 171.2 Wh kg−1, while significantly reducing the difference in the migration numbers of Na+ and ClO4−. Additionally, it demonstrates outstanding cycling stability (96.1% retention after 10 000 cycles). These findings provide a viable new approach for the preparation of high‐performance SICs.

title: Ultrasound‐Activated Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework Synergistically Enhances Antitumor Immunity by Epigenetic Reprogramming and Pyroptosis Induction
content:
This work presents a nanosystem (HDTO) designed to overcome epigenetic suppression of the pyroptosis mediator GSDME. The ultrasound‐activated platform generates radicals to simultaneously release a demethylating agent and activate caspase‐3, converting apoptosis into pyroptosis. This switch potently enhances immunogenic cell death, reprograms the tumor microenvironment, and elevates antitumor immunity, effectively inhibiting tumor progression and metastasis.








ABSTRACT
Pyroptosis, a pro‐inflammatory form of cell death, elicits robust antitumor immune responses. However, pyroptosis‐based cancer immunotherapy is hampered by the epigenetic silencing of gasdermin E (GSDME) through hypermethylation of the DFNA5 gene. To overcome this limitation, we engineered an innovative nanosystem by first synthesizing a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive decitabine prodrug (DTO), which was subsequently encapsulated within hydrogen‐bonded organic frameworks to form the HDTO nanoplatform. Upon ultrasound (US) activation, the HDTO nanoplatform exhibited potent ROS generation, enabling two complementary functions: (1) triggering decitabine release to demethylate DFNA5 and restore GSDME expression and (2) activating caspase‐3, thereby initiating the caspase‐3/GSDME‐mediated pyroptotic pathway. This apoptosis‐to‐pyroptosis switching mechanism significantly enhanced immunogenic cell death and potentiated antitumor immunity. In vivo studies demonstrated that US‐activated HDTO induced robust pyroptosis, remodeled the tumor microenvironment, and elicited superior antitumor immune responses, resulting in marked suppression of tumor growth and metastasis. Single‐cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that HDTO + US‐induced pyroptosis depleted nonimmune cells while expanding monocyte and neutrophil populations, demonstrating effective immunoreprogramming. This study establishes a novel therapeutic paradigm that synergistically integrates epigenetic modulation with pyroptosis induction to enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
content:
A Co/Co7Fe3 heterostructure is designed to drive electrocatalytic nitrate reduction via a unique [4+4] tandem mechanism. The interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerates water dissociation, and enables hydrogen spillover. Its heterointerfaces optimize the adsorption energetics of key intermediates, and its synergistic dual spillover enhances the reaction, delivering a high NH3 yield rate with nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency.








ABSTRACT
Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO3−) reduction reaction (NO3RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co7Fe3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO3RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4‐electron step reduces NO3− to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4‐electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4‐electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co7Fe3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO3RR through synergistic dual‐spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near‐unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h−1 cm−2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn‐nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm−2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
content:
An additive‐mediated sequential crystallization strategy is developed to decouple the formation of Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 phases. This approach drives the detrimental Cs4PbBr6 phase to the film surface, simultaneously improving CsPbBr3 crystallinity and enhancing light outcoupling. Near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield and an outstanding external quantum efficiency of 35.3% are achieved in green perovskite light‐emitting diodes.








ABSTRACT
Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high‐performance perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next‐generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs4PbBr6 phase often accompanies CsPbBr3 crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive‐mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3‐carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3‐CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr3 formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr3 phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs4PbBr6 phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: Contact Resistance at Interfaces Buried Within Organic Transistors Imaged Using Scanning Microwave Impedance Microscopy
content:
Scanning microwave impedance microscopy (sMIM) is introduced here as a new characterization technique for imaging contact resistance at buried metal electrode/organic interfaces. sMIM reveals depletion regions at both Schottky and theoretically Ohmic contacts, with Fermi level pinning confirmed as the origin in the latter. Rather than eliminating contact resistance, it is exploited to develop organic source‐gated transistors with low‐voltage saturation.








ABSTRACT
Contact resistance has been a consistent challenge in the 40‐year history of the organic thin‐film transistor (OTFT). The problem arises because contact resistance at the metal electrode/organic interface is an amalgamation of physical phenomena: From ubiquitous defect states and Fermi level pinning, to the energy difference between the electrode work function and semiconductor transport level. Here, an original approach is taken to address the established OTFT contact resistance challenge. First, a new characterization technique, scanning microwave impedance microscopy (sMIM), is introduced for imaging buried metal electrode/organic interfaces. sMIM indicates contact resistance is arguably intrinsic in certain metal electrode/organic systems; namely, contact resistance exists when charge injection is theoretically Ohmic. The latter is explained by Fermi level pinning far from the organic semiconductor ionization energy, which is confirmed using ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS). Second, organic source‐gated transistors (OSGTs) are developed by exploiting contact resistance as a design principle. OSGTs made from small‐molecule/polymer blends, using 2,8‐difluoro‐5,11‐triethylsilylethynyl anthradithiophene (diF‐TES ADT) and poly(triarylamine) (PTAA), show distinct, low‐voltage saturation, while temperature‐dependent measurements indicate localized carriers govern charge transport. Overall, combining a new measurement technique with novel transistor operating mechanisms leads to a new approach for addressing the complex, and established, contact resistance challenge.

title: Nanoarchitectonics With Static‐Dynamic Synergistic Interfacial Remediation for Practical Zinc Metal Batteries
content:
Static–dynamic interfacial remediation couples a preconstructed In/Sb layer with responsive In3+ electrolyte regulation to stabilize Zn deposition and compensate evolving interfacial defects. The synergistic interface enables nearly 6000 h symmetric‐cell cycling, 95% Zn utilization, and over 3600 h operation of 1 Ah Br2/Zn pouch cells, offering a practical route to durable aqueous zinc batteries.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc metal batteries are promising for large‐scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost, yet their practical deployment remains limited by dendrite growth, parasitic reactions, and the gradual failure of interfacial protection during prolonged cycling. Here, we report a static‐dynamic synergistic interfacial remediation strategy in which a preconstructed In/Sb interfacial layer is coupled with a dynamically responsive electrolyte additive to mitigate continuous interfacial degradation. Specifically, a dual‐phase In/Sb composite layer (ISZ) is formed on Zn by spontaneous galvanic replacement, providing a compact and chemically stable interface that promotes uniform Zn deposition and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, In3+ in the electrolyte dynamically participates in anode‐side regulation during cycling, assisting defect‐responsive interfacial regeneration. Owing to this synergy, the ISZ‐In3+ system delivers both improved initial deposition behavior and sustained interfacial stability during repeated plating/stripping. Symmetric cells operate stably for nearly 6000 h at low areal capacity, for about 500 h under 40 mA cm−2/20 mAh cm−2, and for over 1000 h at an ultrahigh Zn utilization rate of 95%. This strategy is further extended to Br2/Zn batteries, where pouch cells stably operate for nearly 3600 h and 700 h at areal capacities of 12.5 and 25 mAh cm−2, respectively. In addition, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling over 3600 h, and a low‐N/P pouch cell (N/P = 1.46) cycles for nearly 1400 h, while a 400 mAh pouch cell achieves a component‐level energy density of about 80 Wh kg−1, excluding the electrolyte and pouch packaging. This work provides a practical interfacial design strategy for high‐capacity, long‐life aqueous Zn batteries.

title: Synthesis of Bulk Superconducting LiNbO2 Crystals Through CaH2 Reduction
content:
CaH2 reduction reconstructively transforms insulating LiNbO3 single crystals into superconducting bulk LiNbO2 with a critical temperature of Tc = 14.4 K. Scanning electron microscopy reveals large‐volume, high‐yield phase conversion. Magnetization measurements demonstrate a robust ∼ 77% Meissner shielding fraction, establishing bulk superconductivity in this layered niobate system and opening new pathways for synthesis of oxide superconductors.








ABSTRACT
We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO3 single crystals via CaH2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO2, which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, Tc onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole‐doped through de‐lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non‐topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.

title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress‐ROS‐Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy
content:
An ER‐regulating heterojunction converts pathological oxidative cues into directional electron transfer toward bacterial membranes, disrupting bacterial bioenergetics while avoiding additional oxidative burden. Concurrent activation of selenoprotein metabolism restores redox‐ER homeostasis and reshapes the osteoimmune microenvironment, integrating bacterial elimination with host stress regulation to promote periodontal regeneration.








ABSTRACT
In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress‐centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER‐regulating heterojunction (ERR‐HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti3C2 MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti3C2 heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H2O2 to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK‐CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue‐regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR‐HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self‐perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection‐associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle inhibition.

title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
content:
Cathode polarization in anode‐free sodium batteries governs sodium deposition through electric‐field coupling. Cathode‐specific charging suppresses polarization during charging, homogenizes sodium growth, improves Na plating/stripping reversibility, enhances cycling stability across different cathodes, and enables durable pouch cells with high practical energy density.








ABSTRACT
Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode‐free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode‐targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode‐specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)‐dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record‐high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg−1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode‐free full cells based on Na4Fe3(PO4)2 (NFPP), Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), and NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow‐Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
content:
Due to the strong interfacial polarization and reversible charge trapping generated by covalently tethered zwitterion dipoles, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate) (PVIPS) facilitates robust coupling between electro‐ and multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic synaptic transistors achieve ultralow energy consumption of 10.95 aJ per event and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation and pedestrian motion prediction.








ABSTRACT
Neuromorphic in‐sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co‐localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation–anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion‐migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo‐modulation is further attenuated by exciton–polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion‐migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro‐ and photo‐synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation–anion pair prevents long‐distance ion‐migration, ensuring strong cation–anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic modulation coupled with electro‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian‐speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing‐computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
content:
The central role of both electronically interacting and noninteracting chromophores in the photogeneration of charges has been unambiguously identified by ultrafast pump‐probe spectroscopy in thin films of the prototypical non‐fullerene acceptor Y6. Onsager‐like autoionization from higher‐energy excitations on Y6 aggregates is found to control polaron generation with moderate yields.








ABSTRACT
In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.

title: Functional Group Transposition Enables Antiparallel–Parallel Packing Switching in Dithieno[3,2‐b:2′,3′‐d]pyrrole Self‐Assembled Molecules for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
content:
The transposition of trifluoromethyl and chlorine groups on the phenyl termini switches the molecular stacking of the dithienopyrrole‐based acceptor–donor–acceptor type self‐assembled molecules from a disordered antiparallel to a well‐ordered parallel motif. This programmable assembly facilitates the formation of an energetically favorable interface and optimized active‐layer morphology, leading to high‐performance organic photovoltaics, including solar cells with a 20.92% efficiency and photodetectors with a 6.52 × 1014 Jones detectivity.








ABSTRACT
Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium‐tin‐oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole‐transport‐layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor–donor–acceptor type self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho‐/para‐ positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well‐ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot‐noise‐limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 1014 Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 1013 Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state‐of‐the‐art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm2). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co‐engineers interfacial order and active‐layer morphology toward high‐performance organic optoelectronics.

title: GaSex Nanoparticles Modulate Neutrophil Function and Mitigate NET‐Driven Osteogenic Impairment in Osteomyelitis Therapy
content:
Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) emerge as a critical repair‐limiting factor in osteomyelitis, driving osteoblast mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitophagy. Gallium–selenium nanoparticles (GaSex) scavenge reactive oxygen species, redirect neutrophils from NETosis toward bactericidal phagocytosis, eliminate methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, restoring bone regeneration in infected defects.








ABSTRACT
Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis‐associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in Prkn‐knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin‐dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium–selenium nanoparticles (GaSex) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET‐driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair‐limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSex as a redox‐regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.

title: Magneto‐Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics
content:
Magnetic micromotors actively capture and catalytically convert polystyrene micro/nanoplastics into valuable benzoic acid with near‐complete conversion and ∼60% yield. Their magnetic‐field‐driven motion enriches plastic particles, while Au‐generated electromagnetic hot spots enable real time SERS tracking down to 0.17 µg/mL. A machine learning model (R2 = 1.0) accurately predicts degradation performance across diverse water matrices.








ABSTRACT
The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical‐Mn/N‐doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time‐resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near‐complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au‐micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N‐doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO4•‒‐mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate‐determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale‐up conditions, with a machine learning model (R2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno‐economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value‐added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.

title: Spontaneous Capture, Enrichment, and SERS Sensing of Polystyrene Micro/Nanoplastics Enabled by Condensed Plasmonic Coacervate Droplets
content:
Plasmonic coacervate microdroplets, formed through PDDA/ATP liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) and loaded with AgNPs, spontaneously capture and enrich polystyrene micro/nanoplastics from river water, tap water, and water contacted with PS cups and EPS containers. This enrichment enables sensitive surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection and signal enhancement, offering a promising route for monitoring micro/nanoplastics in real‐world water samples.








ABSTRACT
Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co‐encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three‐dimensional droplet‐confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 109, excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano‐ and micro‐scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food‐contact materials.

title: Hollow Conjugated Microporous Polymers Anchored With ZnxCd1‐xS Quantum Dots: An Additive‐Free Photocatalyst for H2O2 Synthesis via S‐Scheme Charge Transfer
content:
An S‐scheme ZCS@hPSe heterojunction is constructed for additive‐free photocatalytic H2O2 production in pure water. The interface synergy, hollow mass transfer, and S‐scheme charge separation collectively deliver a rate of 15.13 mmol g−1 h−1 with a synergy factor of 1.53, surpassing pristine counterparts and offering a promising route for sustainable photosynthesis.








ABSTRACT
Photocatalytic H2O2 production via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, but single‐component photocatalysts suffer from rapid charge recombination. Here, we construct an S‐scheme heterojunction by growing ZnxCd1‐xS (ZCS) quantum dots (QDs) in situ on hollow conjugated microporous polymers (CMPs) containing selenadiazole units (hPSe). The hollow CMPs scaffold provides high surface area, abundant pores for QDs embedding, efficient mass transfer, and enhanced light harvesting, while the selenadiazole units promote strong interfacial coupling. In pure water without any sacrificial agent, the optimal ZCS@hPSe‐2 composite achieved an outstanding H2O2 production rate of 15.13 mmol g−1 h−1 with a synergy factor of 1.53 and an apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 8.82% at 400 nm, operating exclusively via the 2e− ORR. The dramatic performance is attributed to the S‐scheme charge transfer mechanism, which preserves the strong redox potentials of both components and suppresses bulk charge recombination. This work demonstrates that rational integration of QDs with hollow CMPs provides a viable pathway toward efficient, additive‐free photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis.

title: Supramolecular Adhesives with Tunable Crystallinity for Extreme Environments
content:
Facile thermal complexation of tannic acid and PCL yields a solvent‐free supramolecular hot‐melt adhesive. It remains flexible at cryogenic temperatures and exhibits robust bonding stability in harsh aqueous and organic environments, enabling 3D shaping applications.








ABSTRACT
Developing high‐performance adhesives capable of withstanding harsh environments‐specifically ultralow temperatures, water, acid, base and organic solvents‐via low‐cost, scalable manufacturing remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the architecture of spider silk, we report a facile strategy to fabricate a solvent‐free supramolecular adhesive composed of tannic acid (TA) and poly(ε‐caprolactone) (PCL). Integrated theoretical and experimental investigations uncover the critical role of crystallinity modulation in governing adhesion performance. The resulting adhesive achieves an exceptional strength of up to 8.5 MPa at ambient temperature (25°C) and 6.6 MPa at cryogenic temperature (−196°C), outperforming existing commercial hot‐melt adhesives. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable stability in corrosive underwater environments (acidic, alkaline, and saline) and organic solvents. This work not only establishes a novel bioinspired design paradigm for adhesives operating under extreme conditions but also paves the way for the scalable production and practical applications of supramolecular materials.

title: Industry‐Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET‐Cu Current Collectors
content:
Metallized plastic Cu current collectors offer lightweight alternatives but suffer from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) degradation and interfacial failure. Here, an industry‐scalable Al2O3 layer is introduced to protect the PET substrate and stabilize Cu||PET interfaces, enabling robust current collectors with improved electrochemical reliability and long‐term cycling stability for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries under harsh operating conditions.








ABSTRACT
Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al2O3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min−1, substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al2O3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al2O3‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al2O3‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.

title: Programmable Structural Color Lifetimes via Activation Energy Engineering for Spatiotemporally Encoded Dynamic Optical Encryption
content:
Marangoni effect‐driven surface gratings with dynamically decaying amplitudes were fabricated. By controlling the activation energy and initial amplitude, time‐programmable structural color encryption materials with unprecedented lifetimes spanning from 300 s to over 240 days were developed. Leveraging this tunability, stimulus‐responsive optical encryption, time‐resolved multilevel information encryption, and practical cold‐chain integrity monitoring were demonstrated, collectively enhancing the security and information capacity of structural color encryption materials.








ABSTRACT
Spatiotemporally programmable structural color holds great promise for high‐security optical encryption, yet precisely tailoring the lifetime of structural color across a broad temporal range spanning multiple orders of magnitude remains a significant challenge in polymer systems. The lifetime of structural color is intrinsically governed by the segmental relaxation kinetics of the underlying polymer network, which has been largely overlooked in the rational design. Here, we report a dynamic surface grating with programmable structural color lifetime, in which the optical evolution process is precisely encoded by tuning the activation energy through crosslinking density and amplitude control. Driven by segmental relaxation, the grating amplitude gradually decays over time, redistributing diffracted energy back to specular reflection and causing a gradual fading of structural color. By spatially encoding the relaxation activation energy via photomask‐assisted UV exposure, the structural color lifetime governed by local amplitude decay kinetics can be independently programmed across different regions, spanning an unprecedented temporal range from 300 s to over 240 days. This strategy enables diverse applications, ranging from stimulus‐responsive optical encryption and time‐resolved multilevel information encryption to practical cold‐chain integrity monitoring, establishing activation energy as a broadly applicable handle for temporal programmability in dynamic optical systems.

title: Design of Bridging‐Oxygen‐Modulated Fe–Ni Dual‐Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
content:
Our work presents a robust dual‐atomic‐site catalyst for electrochemical oxygen redox and it's multiply stable mechanism via bridge‐O‐triggered electron and geometry regulation on atom‐scale, which can simultaneously resist the poison effect by H2O2 during ORR and electrochemical etch during OER. The advanced catalyst exhibits an unconventionally durable operation life exceeding 2800 h in reversible zinc‐air battery cathodes.








ABSTRACT
Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long‐term stability of metal‐nitrogen‐carbon atomic‐site catalysts (M–N–Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi–N–C dual‐atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ2‐O electron modulator for long‐life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O‐coordinated vicinal Fe–Ni configuration. The µ2‐O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N‐site protonation and intermediate‐induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H2O2/ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination‐engineering strategy for designing durable M–N–C catalysts for long‐life RZABs.

title: Self‐Segregated Buried‐Interface Regulation Resolves Kinetic–Environmental Coupling for Ambient Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Here, in situ photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals that delayed buried‐interface phase conversion induces kinetic decoupling, triggering interfacial defect buildup and preferential moisture invasion. A self‐segregated NFA synchronizes dual‐interface crystallization. Optimized flexible perovskite solar cells achieve a champion PCE of 24.84% (certified 23.75%) and retain 96.26% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85 ± 5% RH.








ABSTRACT
Ambient fabrication of flexible perovskite solar cells is fundamentally limited by a detrimental kinetic–environmental coupling at the buried interface, where moisture ingress and nonoptimal crystallization mutually compromise film quality—yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using dual‐side in situ photoluminescence, we overturn the conventional top–down model by revealing simultaneous nucleation at both gas–liquid and liquid–solid interfaces during antisolvent‐assisted solution processing, but find that outward solvent evaporation delays α‐phase conversion at the buried interface relative to the surface, creating kinetic mismatch that exacerbates moisture attack and defect accumulation. To address these kinetic and environmental constraints, we design a self‐segregating multifunctional molecule, 2‐[(3‐trifluoromethyl)phenyl]amino‐3‐pyridinecarboxylic acid (NFA), which spontaneously enriches at the buried interface to synchronize dual‐interface crystallization while simultaneously passivating defects, optimizing energy‐level alignment, and constructing a hydrophobic barrier against moisture ingress. Consequently, this self‐segregated kinetic–environmental regulation yields record ambient flexible photovoltaic performance with power‐conversion efficiencies of 24.84% (0.09 cm2, certified at 23.75%) and 21.46% on mini‐modules (13.8 cm2). The optimized devices maintain 96.26% of their starting efficiency following 1000 h damp aging at 85 ± 5% RH. Our work establishes self‐segregated interfacial regulation as a rational route to address kinetic and environmental constraints in scalable flexible photovoltaics.

title: Grain‐Boundary‐Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity‐Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
content:
Grain‐boundary‐rich palladium enables catalytic hydrogen sensing under extreme humidity by accelerating PdHx formation, weakening water adsorption, and sustaining H2–O2 reactivity. The resulting sensor operates without external heating across 22°C–80°C and up to 90% relative humidity while maintaining high sensitivity, selectivity, stability, and robust quantitative performance under dynamically varying environmental conditions.








ABSTRACT
Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity‐tolerant catalytic H2 sensor based on a grain‐boundary‐rich palladium nanostructure (PdGB) that operates without any external heating. The PdGB sensor functions reliably at 22°C–80°C and 0%–90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m−3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000‐fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H2), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine‐learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature‐programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdHx formation for weakening H2O adsorption and suppress humidity‐induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials‐design strategy for next‐generation humidity‐tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

title: In Situ Constructed Pore‐Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide‐Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High‐Fidelity Signal Transmission
content:
A pore‐chain interlocked polyimide/COF network is constructed using amino‐functionalized hollow COFs as molecular anchoring nodes. The interlocked interface restricts segmental motion and stabilizes the oriented fibrous architecture, enabling an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50, dielectric loss of 0.001, stable dielectric performance up to 250°C, and markedly enhanced high‐frequency signal transmission and crosstalk suppression for advanced electronic applications.








ABSTRACT
The ultralow k porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the k‐tanδ trade‐off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H‐TD‐COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore‐chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino‐functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long‐range charge migration pathways while preserving stress‐transfer and heat‐dissipation continuity. The resulting PI‐g‐COF(4) nanocomposites with 4 wt% H‐TD‐COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device‐level measurements further reveal a signal‐to‐noise‐and‐distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow k dielectrics.

title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
content:
Amorphous organic anodes paired with CuFe‐PBA cathodes enable pouch cells delivering 1.14 V and 1.037 Ah, marking an Ah‐level breakthrough for AAIBs.








ABSTRACT
The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8‐tetraamino‐5,10‐dihydrophenazine‐1,4,6,9‐tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m2 g−1, delivers 242.8 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR‐FTIR and EQCM‐D measurements reveal that NH4+ is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH4+ accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H3O+ for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe‐PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Moreover, the first Ah‐level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

title: Carbonyl‐Site‐Mediated Oxygen Reduction in Fluorenone‐Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis
content:
Fluorenone carbonyls act as dynamic molecular active sites in COFs for photocatalytic H2O2 production, which trap photogenerated electrons to generate persistent ketyl radical‐anion‐like states that promote O2 activation. This generalizable carbonyl‐centered strategy enables efficient H2O2 photosynthesis across in water, salt‐containing solutions with achieving an AQY of 30.40% at pH 13 and biphasic systems with up to 39.3 mmol·g−1·h−1.








ABSTRACT
Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) photosynthesis from molecular oxygen and water offers a sustainable route for decentralized oxidant generation, yet elucidating the molecular‐level active sites for oxygen activation in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains challenging. Herein, we report a fluorenone‐containing COF, FO‐Tp, as an efficient photocatalyst for H2O2 production, delivering a rate nearly ten times higher than that of fluorene‐based COF, highlighting the crucial contribution of fluorenone carbonyls to photocatalytic oxygen reduction. The fluorenone carbonyls facilitate photogenerated‐electron trapping and the formation of persistent electron‐rich radical states with ketyl radical‐anion‐like character, enabling FO‐Tp to maintain excellent H2O2 production under alkaline conditions (AQY = 30.40%, pH = 13, at 400 nm) and in concentrated salt solutions. Extended fluorenone‐based COFs validate the generality of this active‐site design, reaching 2478.1 µmol·g−1 h−1 in pure water and up to 38.6 mmol g−1·h−1 in a water/benzyl alcohol biphasic system. Spectroscopic experiments and density functional theory calculations jointly confirm the reduced fluorenone carbonyl as a thermodynamically favored and generalizable electron‐accumulating active site for oxygen reduction to H2O2. This work elucidates how the fluorenone carbonyl functions as a dynamic molecular active site and proposes a strategy for designing efficiently H2O2‐producing COF photocatalysts by incorporating carbonyl activation.

title: Atomic‐Level Regulating Layer‐by‐Layer Zinc Deposition by High‐Entropy Single‐Atoms Electrolyte Additive
content:
The micropore high‐entropy single‐atom carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) are synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to accelerate the migration kinetics of Zn2+ for suppressing interfacial Zn2+ concentration polarization and strengthening Zn chemistry at the atomic level, resulting in layer‐by‐layer Zn deposition. 








ABSTRACT
Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid‐solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy‐dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high‐entropy single‐atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn2+ concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn2+ transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn2+ from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn2+ flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn2+ supersaturation and guiding layer‐by‐layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm−2, and 800 h even at 50 mA cm−2, with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm−2. Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal‐ion batteries.

title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal‐Bacteria Interactions
content:
It is well established that the antibacterial properties of metals have tremendous importance for bioengineering applications. What is not as appreciated, however, is the reproducibility crisis in this field's vast literature. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations.








ABSTRACT
The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever‐increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source‐specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross‐laboratory validation.

title: MitoDART: Mitochondria‐Targeted Intracellular DNA Assembly for Selective Mitochondrial Interference and Early Molecular Response Monitoring
content:
In this study, we report a mitochondria‐targeted dual‐biomarker‐activated intracellular DNA assembly for mitochondrial regulation and tracking (Mito‐DART), which enables cell‐selective mitochondrial interference and in situ monitoring of early molecular responses following mitochondrial disruption.








ABSTRACT
Rational modulation of mitochondrial functions to reprogram cellular behavior and fate has emerged as a promising therapeutic paradigm. However, it is still challenging to achieve cell‐selective mitochondrial interference with in situ monitoring of early molecular responses. In this study, we report a mitochondria‐targeted dual‐biomarker‐activated intracellular DNA assembly for mitochondrial regulation and tracking (Mito‐DART), which enables cell‐selective interference of mitochondria and in situ biosensing for early assessment of molecular responses. Based on the AND logic responsive to two tumor biomarkers, apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) and microRNAs, Mito‐DART is specifically activated in tumor cells and undergoes hybridization chain reaction (HCR)‐driven DNA assembly, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis‐associated cellular responses. More importantly, Mito‐DART enables in situ monitoring of cytochrome c (Cyt c) release, an early molecular marker of mitochondria‐mediated apoptosis, within 1 h following mitochondrial disruption, providing an early molecular readout of mitochondria‐mediated apoptotic signaling that complements conventional tissue‐level endpoint assessments. Overall, this design provides a programmable framework for biomarker‐gated mitochondrial intervention that combines selective activation with built‐in assessment of downstream molecular responses.

title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
content:
An aqueous all‐organic battery combining a PTCDI anode with an organic bromine cathode achieves a high‐discharge voltage of 2.0 V through reversible Br−/Br0/Br+ conversion, together with high‐energy and power densities. The battery accommodates diverse charge carriers, while electrolyte anions regulate electrode reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect, and cations primarily govern reaction kinetics.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous all‐organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high‐working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10‐perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary‐ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two‐electron bromine conversion (Br−/Br0/Br+). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li+, Na+, K+, NH4+, Ca2+, and Mg2+. We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active‐material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one‐electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two‐electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg−1 based on the combined electrode active‐material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm−2 further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high‐energy AOBs.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
content:
A paired electrochemical PVC upcycling strategy combines cathodic dechlorination with anodic synthesis of novel nitrogen‐containing cyclic acetals as precursors for poly(amino ester) synthesis. Experimental and computational studies reveal that heteroatoms strongly influence cyclization efficiencies of medium‐sized rings. The methodology unlocks access to biodegradable poly(amino ester) homo‐ and copolymer synthesis via radical ring‐opening polymerization. 








ABSTRACT
A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
content:
The first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is reported. A wide range of alkenes underwent highly efficient enantioselective dihydroxylation under ball‐milling conditions, typically reaching completion within 30 min to afford the corresponding chiral diols in good to high yield with excellent enantioselectivity.








ABSTRACT
The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution‐based conditions (typically water/t‐BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional‐group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution‐based conditions, including poorly soluble, base‐sensitive, and catalyst‐coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram‐scale synthesis.
