title: A General Strategy to Identify Impurity‐Activated Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Synthetic Triarylamines
content:
A sequential diagnostic framework integrating synthetic‐route validation, chromatographic fractionation, purification, impurity identification, and reconstitution is established to distinguish intrinsic RTP from impurity‐derived emission in synthetic triarylamines. Trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during synthesis are identified as a major class of triplet‐energy traps that activate RTP of the synthesized triarylamines.








ABSTRACT
Distinguishing intrinsic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) from impurity‐derived emission remains challenging in organic luminescent materials, particularly when trace emissive species evade routine characterization. Herein, we establish a diagnostic framework for identifying impurity‐activated RTP in synthetic triarylamines through route‐, fraction‐, and purification‐dependent validation, impurity reconstitution, and theoretical analysis. Using TPA, TPAO, and related heteroatom‐engineered triarylamines as representative systems, we show that nominally identical samples can exhibit different RTP behaviors depending on synthetic history and purification extent, despite appearing chemically indistinguishable by conventional analyses. Progressive purification induces blue‐shifted and narrowed emissions and ultimately eliminates afterglow, revealing hidden emissive species. Structural analyses identify trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during metal‐catalyzed coupling reactions as a representative class of RTP‐active impurities. Reintroduction of independently synthesized impurity candidates into rigorously purified hosts restores phosphorescence, providing direct functional evidence that synthesis‐derived byproducts can activate RTP. Theoretical calculations further show that these impurities possess lower‐lying triplet states and act as triplet‐energy traps. Extension of the workflow to related synthetic triarylamines reproduces purification‐dependent RTP loss and impurity‐enabled recovery, supporting the applicability of this strategy across the triarylamine systems examined here and establishing synthetic history and purification as critical variables in assigning the origin of organic RTP.

title: Tailoring the Na+ Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
content:
A phosphorus‐rich interphase on NP‐HC captures PF6− anions near the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP), creating an anion‐rich interfacial environment. This tailored interface promotes rapid Na+ desolvation and accelerates interfacial ion‐migration kinetics, overcoming sluggish desolvation and transport in conventional hard carbon (HC) and enabling improved low‐temperature electrochemical performance.








ABSTRACT
Na+ desolvation and diffusion across the solid‐electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard‐carbon sodium‐ion batteries. Here, we design an anion‐capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus‐rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built‐in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na+ interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP‐HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP‐HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP‐HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium‐ion batteries under harsh conditions.

title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
content:
Water‐induced phase transformations challenge molecular crystals stability, yet their pathways remain elusive. Using piroxicam as a model, a multistage pathway is revealed where an amorphous phase serves as a critical intermediate. Targeting this intermediate, enables kinetic control of transformation by surfactant chain length. This work establishes a foundation for rational design of additives to regulate phase behavior in organic crystals.








ABSTRACT
Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl‐chain lengths. Longer‐chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive‐interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V2AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
content:
Built‐in electric fields are constructed at the heterogeneous interfaces of V2AlC‐derived magnetic‐dielectric composites to modulate interfacial charge dynamics. These fields enhance multiple polarization, optimize impedance matching, and strengthen attenuation. Consequently, the heterostructures achieve a broad effective absorption bandwidth of 6.72 GHz and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB. 








ABSTRACT
The tailored design of magnetic‐dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high‐performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al2O3 heterostructures with built‐in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V2AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox‐potential‐driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work‐function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface‐potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect‐induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high‐performance broadband microwave absorbers.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
content:
This work demonstrates an effective strategy to achieve narrowband organic ultralong afterglow by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization. Through engineering multiresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence guests, the full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours are achieved.








ABSTRACT
Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) guests, we achieve full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR‐TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m2, an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record‐breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next‐generation OUA materials.

title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoOx Surfaces
content:
Cobalt‐based model catalysts are designed to investigate their oxidation‐state‐dependent catalytic roles during urea electrosynthesis from CO2 and NO2−. Cr3+ retards CoOx over‐reduction, stabilizing a non‐equilibrium Co/CoOx working surface. Our results suggest a spatially coupled reaction network: metallic Co tends to form CO2‐derived *CO, CoOx motifs may generate *NH2, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO–*NH2 coupling toward urea.








ABSTRACT
Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO2 and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt‐based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr3+ to retard cathodic over‐reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non‐equilibrium Co/CoOx surface under working conditions. The optimized Co@CoOx‐Cr1 catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 40.1 ± 1.1% and a yield rate of 102.27 ± 3.31 mmol h−1 gcat−1 under pressurized CO2 at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation‐state‐dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO2‐to‐*CO conversion, stabilized CoOx motifs may promote *NH2 formation, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO─*NH2 coupling for urea formation. This work identifies the controlled stabilization of coexisting phases with distinct oxidation states as a strategy for steering selectivity in multi‐reactant electrocatalysis.

title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
content:
Spectrally resolved single‐molecule imaging of Nile Red enables membrane‐order analysis at the single‐vesicle level, revealing substantial heterogeneity in cholesterol content among extracellular vesicles.








ABSTRACT
Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order‐resolved, spectrally encoded super‐resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single‐EV level. Combining Nile Red single‐molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle‐to‐vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell‐type‐ and tissue‐dependent differences. Most cancer‐cell‐derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non‐tumor counterparts, although MDA‐MB‐231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin‐mediated to non‐clathrin‐mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer‐cell‐derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single‐EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV‐mediated intercellular communication.

title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
content:
Coordination‐driven self‐assembly integrates multivalent lectin recognition, porphyrin‐based photosensitization, and aqueous solubility within a single, well‐defined nanocage, enabling galectin‐targeted photodynamic activity in cancer cells.








ABSTRACT
Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible‐light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)‐anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination‐driven subcomponent self‐assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe8L6 architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc‐metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [1‐Zn][BF4]16, generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red‐light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high‐affinity binding to galectin‐3 (Kd = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [1‐Zn][BF4]16 exhibited potent light‐induced cytotoxicity with negligible dark toxicity, with a phototoxicity index (PI) of 55, while pre‐treatment with lactose or thiodigalactose was protective against [1‐Zn][BF4]16 toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination‐driven self‐assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

title: Boosting DMF Electrosynthesis Over Bifunctional NiCo Catalysts via Methanol‐Supplemented *CHO Supply
content:
This work developed a NiCo bimetallic catalyst that undergoes in situ reconstruction to form NiOOH/CoOOH dual active sites for efficient DMF synthesis from methanol and DMA (56% FE, 518 µmol cm−2 h−1, 105 h stability), with methanol supplying additional *CHO source to boost C−N coupling.








ABSTRACT
Traditional industrial routes for N,N‐dimethylformamide (DMF) synthesis typically require harsh conditions of high temperature and pressure, leading to high energy consumption and a large carbon footprint. Electrosynthesis of DMF has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, this pathway still faces the challenges of low activity and poor selectivity. In this study, we present an efficient bifunctional NiCo electrocatalyst synthesized via the electrodeposition method. This catalyst achieves a DMF Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 56% with a production rate of 518 µmol cm−2 h−1. Combined in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that NiOOH and CoOOH species act as potent oxygen‐transfer mediators, facilitating N–H bond activation and dehydrogenation of dimethylamine (DMA). These species also promote C–N coupling between the *N(CH3)2 intermediate and *CHO intermediates derived from both methanol and the self‐decomposition of DMA. Furthermore, we find that the introduction of methanol provides a sufficient supply of *CHO intermediates, thereby further enhancing the selectivity of DMF synthesis compared with using DMA as the sole substrate. This work not only identifies the origin of the *CHO donor and its pivotal function in DMF electrosynthesis but also provides a foundation for designing multicomponent synergistic catalysts for advanced electrosynthesis.

title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO4 Electrodes
content:
We proposed a photocatalytic strategy toward low‐energy repair of spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP) materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation for degradation of PVDF and targeted Li replenishment of LFP. The repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% maintained 98.3% capacity retention ratio after 1500 cycles. 








ABSTRACT
Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low‐energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation. The photogenerated holes promote the formation of •OH radicals, which abstract hydrogen atoms from the methylene units in PVDF, triggering the scission of polymer backbones and thus enabling the effective degradation of PVDF. Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO2 create a strong reductive microenvironment conducive to the reduction of Fe3+ to Fe2+, which reduces the Li+ migration barrier and facilitates lithium replenishment. The TiO2 catalyst can incorporate into the material lattice as a favorable dopant to optimize the performances of as‐repaired LFP material. Specially, the repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% TiO2 delivers a high discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh g−1 at 1 C with 99.8% capacity retention ratio after 100 cycles. Even at a high rate of 5 C, it maintains 98.3% capacity retention ratio over 1500 cycles.

title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
content:
Terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) act as artificial pan‐PIP phosphatases, dephosphorylating plasma‐membrane phosphoinositides to block GSDMD pore formation and inflammasome activation. TCNs suppress pyroptotic cytokine release and improve survival in murine endotoxemic sepsis, establishing nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a strategy for precision pyroptosis attenuation.








ABSTRACT
Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)‐mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice‐induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce3+/Ce4+ ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20‐fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate (para‐nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N‐terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD‐NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This pan‐PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro‐inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
content:
Here we report a Ni/photoredox‐catalyzed three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes that overrides the polarity mismatch to achieve C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent E‐stereoselectivity, enabling access to diverse β‐amino acid derivatives. Mechanistic and DFT studies show that radical addition and C–C reductive elimination control selectivity, with a key hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the diene carbonyl group directing C1 addition.








ABSTRACT
The difunctionalization of conjugated dienes poses a significant challenge in controlling regio‐ and stereoselectivity due to the presence of two conjugated double bonds. Conventional radical addition reactions adhere to the polarity‐matching principle, wherein nucleophilic alkyl radicals preferentially attack the electrophilic C4 position of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes. Consequently, the polarity‐mismatched C1‐selective addition has remained unexplored. Herein, we report a three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes with α‐aminoalkyl radicals and alkyl bromides via dual nickel/photoredox catalysis. This protocol overcomes the inherent polarity‐mismatching effect, achieving unprecedented C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent E‐stereoselectivity. The reaction provides efficient access to structurally diverse β‐amino acid derivatives, featuring broad substrate compatibility and promising utility in the derivatization of complex molecules. Combined mechanistic investigations and DFT calculations reveal that both radical addition and C–C reductive elimination govern the regio‐ and stereoselectivity. Notably, a significant hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the carbonyl group of the 1,3‐diene in the transition state plays a pivotal role in directing the radical addition to the polarity‐mismatched C1 position.

title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
content:
Pyridines are remodeled into regiodefined N‐alkyl pyrazoles through amine‐mediated ring opening and selective two‐carbon extrusion. Preinstallation of the N‐alkyl group programs product regiochemistry, enabling precise ring‐to‐ring skeletal editing and late‐stage access to pyrazole analogues of pyridine‐containing drugs.








ABSTRACT
N‐Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C5N pyridine framework into a C3N2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
content:
Subtle perturbation of the interfacial binding of Cypate on sub‐7 nm UCNPs dramatically modulates triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a highly sensitive upconversion luminescence (UCL) response. Leveraging this signal‐transduction superiority, the TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) achieves a signal‐to‐background ratio of 375 and enables femtogram‐level p24 detection, providing a versatile and ultrasensitive platform for trace biomarker detection.








ABSTRACT
Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV‐1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near‐infrared dye, Cypate, on sub‐7 nm NaGdF4:Yb3+/Er3+ upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal‐to‐background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state‐perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) for HIV‐1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET‐ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL−1, representing an 860‐fold improvement over the corresponding ALP‐based method by employing the identical immunoassay steps, thus enabling early HIV diagnosis within the critical serological window period.

title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
content:
Selective gas‐phase methane oxidation to methanol is achieved over Ag‐decorated GaON/GaN using molecular oxygen or untreated room air. Partial surface oxidation promotes O2 activation, while residual –NH groups regulate oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates, suppressing methanol overoxidation to CO2. This cooperative surface chemistry enables efficient methane‐to‐methanol conversion with high methanol selectivity and production rates.








ABSTRACT
Selective oxidation of methane to methanol using molecular oxygen remains challenging because methane activation is often accompanied by deep oxidation of the desired methanol product. Here we report a metal‐decorated, partially oxidized GaON/GaN photocatalyst for gas‐phase methane‐to‐methanol conversion using molecular oxygen as the oxidant. The optimized Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst delivers a methane oxidation rate of 2.6 mmol g−1 h−1 with ∼85% CH4‐to‐CH3OH selectivity under O2. When untreated room air is used as the oxidant in a closed‐loop recirculating system, the catalyst maintains an activity of 1.0–1.3 mmol g−1 h−1 in a 50 h test, with comparable methanol selectivity. Complementary mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a mechanism in which partial surface oxidation promotes O2 activation, while residual surface –NH species may moderate the resulting reactive intermediates through local H‐transfer processes, thereby suppressing methanol overoxidation. These results highlight partially oxidized oxynitride surfaces as a promising platform for selective methane upgrading under gas‐phase photocatalytic conditions.

title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
content:
A dual‐functional artificial interphase featuring tethered imidazolium cations for electrostatic anion anchoring and long aliphatic side chains for anti‐swelling addresses the critical failure of polymer coatings in localized high‐concentration electrolytes.









ABSTRACT
Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion‐rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self‐sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion‐rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion‐anchoring and anti‐swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE‐favored anion‐rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti‐swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS‐SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li+ transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li2O‐rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether‐, ester‐, and sulfone‐based LHCEs.

title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
content:
Conceptual illustration of a magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filter using a tetravalent cerium complex. The complex exhibits MCD signals spanning the visible spectrum with a sign reversal at ∼520 nm, providing a molecular approach toward panchromatic helicity filters using a single molecular species.








ABSTRACT
Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filters provide a material‐based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f‐orbital‐based ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron‐donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f‐orbital‐based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday B‐term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible‐range light‐helicity filters.

title: Rational Regulation of Ligand Conformation Toward Topology Reconfiguration for Sieving Butane Isomers
content:
A novel cage‐like anion‐pillared metal‐organic framework SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu, constructed via ligand conformation‐directed topology reconfiguration, exhibits outstanding molecular sieving performance for butane isomers.








ABSTRACT
Achieving one‐step purification of n‐C4H10 and iso‐C4H10 from their isomeric mixtures with high efficiency and high purity is highly desirable yet extremely challenging, as it critically necessitates adsorbents that integrate size‐exclusive sieving functionality, high n‐C4H10 adsorption capacity, and fast adsorption kinetics. Herein, we synthesize a novel cage‐like anion‐pillared MOF adsorbent (SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu) through ligand‐conformation‐directed topology reconfiguration. Compared with the pillar‐layer prototype SIFSIX‐TEPE‐Cu, SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu exhibits a distinctive “confined window–expanded cavity” synergistic pore structure, with pore apertures strategically situated between the kinetic diameters of n‐C4H10 and iso‐C4H10, thus enabling size‐exclusive molecular sieving. Furthermore, the large cages and 3D pore architecture confer both a high n‐C4H10 adsorption capacity (46.6 cm3/g) and a rapid adsorption rate (2.3 × 10−12 m2 s−1). Both kinetic analyses and DFT simulations provide mechanistic insights into the preferential adsorption and diffusion of n‐C4H10. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu enables one‐step purification of both n‐C4H10 and iso‐C4H10 from their binary mixture under various conditions, such as high temperatures, high gas flow rates, and high humidities. After one separation cycle, 23.8 L kg−1 high‐purity iso‐C4H10 (>99.99%) and 27.8 L kg−1 n‐C4H10 (>99.0%) can be obtained, respectively.

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
content:
Hydroxyl substitution simultaneously promotes crystallization and affinity‐site formation in hydrazone‐linked covalent organic framework membranes. By moderating framework assembly, reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding, and favoring keto‐enamine tautomerization, hydroxyl groups generate ordered nanochannels and uranyl‐binding pockets. Their combined effects enable preferential Cs+ permeation, Sr2+ exclusion, and affinity‐mediated UO22+ retention within a single membrane.








ABSTRACT
One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs+, Sr2+ and UO22+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO22+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO22+ uptake of 336 mg g−1 and a Cs+ permeation flux of 0.26 mol m−2 h−1, while exhibiting suppressed Sr2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs+/Sr2+ and Cs+/UO22+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: Full‐Process Synergistic Optimization of Buried Interfaces via Molecule‐Assisted Co‐Assembly for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
Through a full‐process synergistic optimization strategy, TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution, anchors onto the NiOx, and co‐assembles with SAMs while optimizing their arrangement and strengthening their anchoring, thereby providing a favorable template for perovskite crystallization as well as regulating the chemical environment of the buried interface. A representative unencapsulated device retains around 97% of initial efficiency after more than 1800 h according to the ISOS‐L‐1 protocol.








ABSTRACT
Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are promising hole‐selective contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet insufficient substrate anchoring and weak buried‐interface interactions limit device efficiency and stability. Here, we report a co‐assembled SAM (Co‐SAM) strategy that enables full‐process synergistic optimization of the perovskite buried interface by introducing tris(4‐fluorophenyl)phosphine oxide (TFPPO) into SAMs. TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution via its strongly polar P═O group and anchors onto NiOx, with its 4‐fluorophenyl arms proposed to interact with unanchored hydroxyl groups of SAMs to strengthen anchoring and refine their arrangement. Furthermore, TFPPO optimizes the interfacial chemical states while serving as an effective template to direct high‐quality perovskite crystal growth. Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the regulated SAMs achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.98% (stabilized PCE of 26.40%) and 20.65% for normal‐bandgap (1.54 eV) and wide‐bandgap (1.78 eV) devices, respectively. Moreover, a representative Co‐SAM‐modified device retains 97% of its initial efficiency after 1856 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and Co‐SAM‐modified devices retain 92.36% of their initial efficiency after 2408 h of continuous aging at 65°C (ISOS‐D‐2).

of Alkenes: Modular Access to Chiral β- and γ-Amino
Esters
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Catalytic alkene difunctionalization is a powerful strategy for the rapid assembly of complex molecular architectures and has wide applications in synthetic chemistry. However, selective construction of two distinct alkyl–alkyl bonds across the C═C bond in alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Existing methods heavily rely on directing group strategy or specific ground-state radical traps, and the regio- and enantioselective dialkylation of alkenes remains elusive. Furthermore, a method enabling the simultaneous access to two regioisomers in an enantioselective manner has not yet been devised. Herein, we present a regioswitchable and enantioselective alkene dialkylation via photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. This approach provides a unique technique for the modular and practical synthesis of optically pure natural and unnatural β- and γ-amino esters, cornerstones of chemistry and biology. This method utilizes readily available and abundant unactivated alkyl halides and protic C(sp3)–H bonds as coupling partners, demonstrating broad substrate applicability as well as excellent regio- and enantioselectivity. The key to the success lies in the ingenious utilization of the rate difference in the generation of alkyl radicals between alkyl iodides and alkyl bromides via halogen-atom transfer. Furthermore, the synthetic practicality of this regiodivergent protocol has been demonstrated in the enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
From Localized Mn Defect
to Oxygen Loss: The Interplay
of Jahn–Teller and Pseudo–Jahn–Teller Distortions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Developing structurally robust layered manganese-based cathodes is pivotal for sodium-ion batteries, yet inhibiting their lattice collapse remains an ongoing challenge. Here, we unravel a previously overlooked degradation mechanism in Na-birnessite, revealing that the localized Pseudo–Jahn–Teller (PJT) distortion exerts a much more catastrophic and dominant impact on framework failure than the traditionally emphasized cooperative Jahn–Teller (JT) effect. We show that during desodiation, the coexistence of structural Mn vacancies and crystal water triggers a strong Mn4+-related PJT distortion, accelerating irreversible oxygen loss at unexpectedly low voltages. To circumvent this vulnerability, we synthesize a Mn-vacancy-suppressed Na0.62Cu0.1Mn0.9O2·0.35H2O cathode. The substantial reduction of Mn vacancies breaks the critical electronic-vibrational coupling pathways, successfully mitigating the localized PJT modes and securing excellent cyclability (80% retention over 1000 cycles). When coupled with a hard carbon anode, the practical viability of this design is fully demonstrated. This discovery shifts the research focus from macro-JT suppression to local-PJT mitigation, establishing an essential guideline for designing degradation-resistant intercalation electrodes.</jats:p>

title:
Chemoselective On-Resin
Synthesis of Imide and Thiosuccinimide
Functionalized Peptides: Enabling Tunable Retro-Thia-Michael Bioconjugations
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report a site-selective synthetic methodology for accessing 5- and 6-membered imide and thiosuccinimide functional groups on-resin via Fmoc solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). The formation of these heterocyclic frameworks is enabled by a modified Corey–Nicolaou activation strategy, which is kinetically favored via a 5/6-exo-trig cyclization according to Baldwin’s rules. The incorporation of the versatile 2-pyridyl thiosuccinimide moiety, acting as a masked maleimide, facilitates chemoselective aqueous solution-phase bioconjugations via a retro-thia-Michael pathway. This platform accommodates a broad scope of peptide modifications, including intramolecular cyclization, peptide stapling, small-molecule/peptide conjugation, and biocompatible protein conjugation. Furthermore, the resulting thiosuccinimide constructs can undergo controlled hydrolysis to yield stable acyclic thioether-linked conjugates, providing uniform peptide derivatives that are highly resistant to subsequent retro-thia-Michael degradation.</jats:p>

title:
Oxygen-Stabilized
Barium Manganese Nitride Framework
Enables Low-Temperature Ammonia Decomposition
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Rational design of stable active sites from earth-abundant elements is essential for replacing precious metals and advancing low-temperature ammonia decomposition for hydrogen delivery. Early 3d transition metals are attractive because of their abundance and low cost, yet their strong nitrogen binding often hinders catalytic turnover. Here, we report a novel oxynitride, Ba6Mn2N6O, in which lattice oxygen coordinates with Ba to stabilize an active barium manganese nitride framework comprising isolated [MnN3]δ− units and electron-confined Ba6 cavities. These Ba6 cavities promote NH3 adsorption and activation, lattice nitrogen enables N–N coupling, and redox-active Mn centers mediate electron transfer from N to H. This cooperative mechanism enables MgO-supported Ba6Mn2N6O to outperform leading nonprecious-metal catalysts and many Ru-based catalysts at 450 °C, while reducing transition-metal costs by 2–4 orders of magnitude relative to Co and Ru. This work demonstrates the potential of rationally engineered, earth-abundant active sites to migrate the reliance on Ru and advance ammonia as a global-scale hydrogen carrier.</jats:p>

Journal of the American

title:
Dissociating
Spin
and Charge Injections in Single-Molecule
Junctions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding the influence of organic radicals on single-molecule conductance is crucial for the development of nanoscale electronic devices. Radical ion systems reported to date typically exhibit both charge and spin effects acting simultaneously in the same manner. In this work, an attempt to separate these two effects is done by exploiting distinct spin injection and charge redistribution behaviors. We synthesized a series of nitronyl nitroxide (NNO) radical derivatives all sharing a common terphenyl conduction pathway. With the inclusion of one NNO unit, the positive charge is delocalized over the terphenyl, whereas the spin remains largely localized. Conversely, for two NNO units, charge injection is disfavored, whereas spin injection is favored, accompanied by a distinct charge redistribution involving the NNO units and the central ring. Using a scanning tunneling microscope break junction (STM-BJ) technique, we find the impacts of these two distinctive situations on the conductance of single-molecule junctions. Introduction of an NNO monoradical gives rise to a 2-fold increase in conductance due to the charge delocalization over the terphenyl. For the diradical, we observe a more substantial 4-fold increase in conductance (from 10–4.56G0 in the nonradical compound to 10–3.95G0), which can be attributed to electronic interaction between the two NNO units. A phenyl spacer is inserted between the NNO radical and the central phenyl ring in the terphenyl, which greatly suppresses the influence of the positive charge and spin effects on the conductance channel. Then, the radical-containing compounds with one and two NNO units present similar conductances emerging from rather different situations. Our findings elucidate the influence mechanisms of molecular structure and spin and charge localization/delocalization on single-molecule conductance, providing valuable insights for enhanced molecular electronic devices.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Wireless Magnetoelectric
Patch Promotes Infected Wound
Scarless Healing by Macrophage Metaboimmune Reprogramming
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Infected cutaneous wounds often lead to fibrotic scarring. Current treatment modalities often fail to dynamically regulate the sequential repair cascade, especially infection control, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Herein, this study develops a remotely controllable therapeutic strategy via a wireless magnetoelectric system. Specifically, a magnetoelectric patch is designed and developed by incorporating magnetoelectric CoFe2O4@BiFeO3 core–shell nanoparticles (CFO@BFO NPs) and a conductive reduced graphene oxide (rGO) network into a hydrogel matrix. Under an external alternating magnetic field, the magnetoelectric patch initially suppresses bacterial survival by inducing oxidative stress, disrupting membrane transporters, and impairing metabolic homeostasis. Subsequently, magnetoelectric stimulation induces the reprogramming of inflammatory macrophages from glycolysis-dominant metabolism to mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) via the PI3K-AKT pathway. Interestingly, this immunometabolic transition is accompanied by the activation of lipid metabolism and efferocytosis pathways for extracellular matrix remodeling. The scarless healing therapeutic effect was validated in mouse full-thickness and rabbit ear wound models. Notably, the magnetoelectric patch outperformed a commercial growth factor dressing in preclinical minipigs, achieving a higher wound healing rate and a reduction in scar-related parameters. Collectively, these findings demonstrate wireless magnetoelectric stimulation as a dynamically controllable therapeutic strategy for coordinating antibacterial and immunometabolic therapies to promote scarless wound healing.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title: Restoration of Rb Tumor Suppressor Function in Retinoblastoma with Intravitreal GPC2-Targeted RB1 mRNA Lipid Nanoparticles
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Loss of RB1, the first identified tumor suppressor gene, is an oncogenic hallmark of retinoblastoma, a malignant pediatric tumor of the developing retina. Restoration of RB1 and consequent reactivation of the Rb tumor suppressor protein represent an ideal gene therapy against the disease. Here, we employed lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) targeting GPC2, a retinoblastoma-specific cell surface antigen, to deliver codon-optimized, synthetic RB1 messenger (m)RNA into retinoblastoma cells. LNPs conjugated to an antibody against GPC2 using strain-promoted azide–alkyne cycloaddition chemistry demonstrated enhanced uptake and expression longevity of mRNA in retinoblastoma cells in vitro and in an intraocular retinoblastoma murine model after intravitreal administration. Mechanistically, Rb tumor suppressor restoration via GPC2-targeted RB1 mRNA-LNPs (aGPC2/LNP-RB1) resulted in decreased retinoblastoma viability in vitro concomitant with global transcriptomic remodeling toward neuronal differentiation after repeated treatments. Critically, clinically achievable doses of intravitreal aGPC2/LNP-RB1 inhibited the growth of intraocular retinoblastoma xenografts in vivo and displayed acute but transient and manageable intraocular inflammation without systemic toxicities in immunocompetent hosts. Collectively, our findings support further development toward clinical translation of aGPC2/LNP-RB1 mRNA therapy for children with refractory intraocular retinoblastoma.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Physics-Structured
Literature Learning Enables Transferable
Ranking and Domain-Aware Prioritization of Carbon Nanotube Growth
Conditions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) enables scalable carbon nanotube (CNT) growth, but synthesis knowledge remains fragmented across catalyst chemistries, growth modes, process conditions, and incompletely reported outcomes, limiting the transfer between studies. Here, we reconstruct 3,496 synthesis records spanning nearly three decades and map each experiment onto a shared physical representation of catalyst and nucleation state, carbon supply, transport, and process boundaries across five CVD growth modes. Cross-paper and chronological validation revealed strongly target-dependent transfer: diameter retained the clearest ranking, with Spearman correlation of 0.737 under paper-grouped cross-validation and 0.609 under chronological holdout, whereas growth quality, IG/ID, orientation, and a multiproperty composite outcome showed weaker or less stable ordering. The physics-structured representation preserved useful ranking information while revealing target-specific reliance on physical descriptors and enabling the consistent reconstruction of candidate states. Conditional quantile predictions and historical replay further showed cutoff-dependent values for prioritizing favorable CNT growth conditions subsequently reported in the literature. Combining these rankings with literature-domain support and foldwise ranking stability yields traceable priorities for experimental evaluation rather than universal or experimentally validated CNT growth recipes.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title: Forward design of thick Fe–N–C cathodes  via  decoupled self-humidification and anti-flooding
content: Fe–N–C catalysts are promising non-platinum-group metal alternatives for proton exchange membrane fuel cells; however, the requisite thick cathode catalyst layers (CCLs) elongate proton-conduction pathways and aggravate liquid-water accumulation, imposing stringent water-management constraints. Here, we develop a quantitative structure–water-management–performance framework by integrating electrochemical characterization with three-dimensional, two-phase, non-isothermal simulations. We identify intra-CCL H+ and O2 transport resistances, rather than intrinsic oxygen reduction kinetics, as the primary architecture-dependent bottlenecks. Mechanistic analysis indicates that self-humidification and anti-flooding are coupled but non-equivalent objectives that follow a volcano-type balance, defining an explicit trade-off for cathode-architecture design. Guided by this principle, a dam-inspired grooved CCL spatially decouples local water retention from liquid-water removal. Gaussian process regression with Bayesian optimization yields a voltage-resolved rule: the optimal groove ratio decreases from 3.96 (high-voltage) to 3.67 (mid-voltage) and 3.30 (low-voltage). Grooved cathodes fabricated at the predicted ratios reproduce this voltage-dependent rule experimentally, and the ranking is retained after 30 000 accelerated-stress-test cycles; a grooved CCL with a 3 : 1 ratio delivers a peak power density approximately 50% higher than the conventional CCL (0.62 versus 0.41 W cm−2 under H2–air). These findings establish a forward-design framework for thick Fe–N–C cathodes, extendable to porous electrochemical electrodes.

title: Tandem Solar Cells Based on Si and Stable Cu(In,Ga)S2 With Efficiency Beyond the Bottom Cell
content:
We present a stable IR transparent widegap sulfide‐chalcopyrite solar cell with certified efficiency of 15.5% and open‐circuit voltage above 1V. Tandem cells with Si and CISe bottom cells are demonstrated, which improve efficiency by 2.5% and 5.0%, respectively. Critical role of Cu‐excess growth and Ag content in determining the absorber quality and photovoltaic performance of sulfide‐chalcopyrite solar cells is discussed.








ABSTRACT
Tandem solar cells require stable, highly efficient top cells with a band gap above 1.6 eV. We present a semitransparent solar cell with an efficiency of 15.52% and an open‐circuit voltage of 1.014 V, based on an environmentally stable sulfide chalcopyrite absorber and ITO back contact. Solar cells are prepared by industrially scalable processes of co‐evaporation, sputter and atomic layer deposition. The progress in efficiency is achieved by alloying with small amounts of Ag (less than 10% of Cu replaced by Ag). Optimum amount of Ag alloying is shown to depend on the amount of Cu‐excess during absorber growth. Ag alloying leads to larger grains, avoids high Ga phases, and reduces non‐radiative recombination, which improves open circuit voltage. Whether the reduction in non‐radiative recombination is due to an increase in net doping or due to a longer minority carrier lifetime appears to depend on the Cu‐excess during process. The efficiency of the top cell remains stable over several months’ storage in a non‐controlled atmosphere. We combine this new top cell in a tandem cell with both Si and CuInSe2 bottom cells, in both cases, the efficiency beyond the bottom cell alone by between 2.5% and 5% absolute.

title: Interphasial Li+ Flux Engineering via Anchoring Vertically Oriented Fluorinated Covalent Organic Frameworks Toward Long‐Cycling Li‐Metal Batteries
content:
Fluorinated covalent organic frameworks layers are directionally anchored onto Li metal to act as artificial solid electrolyte interphases, which bear rapid and homogeneous interphasial Li‐ion transport and uniform Li plating/stripping, thus enabling excellent electrochemical properties. Li‐metal batteries using such modified anodes, including LiFePO4 and LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 coin‐cells, as well as LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch‐cell exhibits greatly enhanced cycling performance compared to countered cells using bare Li anodes.








ABSTRACT
Unstable solid electrolyte interphases and uncontrollable Li‐dendrite growth largely hamper the practical application of metallic Li anode in rechargeable batteries. Constructing a reliable and steady Li interphase is critical to promote commercialization of Li‐metal batteries. In this study, we propose to directionally anchor 2D fluorinated covalent organic frameworks on Li metal to build artificial solid electrolyte interphases, aiming to homogenize and accelerate the interphasial Li+ flux and regulate uniform Li plating/stripping. Theoretical calculations reveal that active fluorine sites with negative electrostatic potential facilitate fast LiTFSI dissociation and strong Li+ adsorption, and oriented 2D channels with low diffusion energy barrier endow high Li+ flux and fast Li+ transport. The obtained interphase has a homogeneously amorphous structure with high mechanical elasticity and thermodynamic stability, exhibiting high compatibility with metallic Li and enabling excellent electrochemical properties. Consequently, its symmetrical cell demonstrates an ultralong cycle life over 1300 h. When paired with commercial cathodes, LiFePO4 cell and LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 cell demonstrate a cycle‐life of 335 and 228 at 5 C, respectively. Notably, 1 Ah LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2//modified Li pouch‐cell exhibits a long cycle‐life over 325 at 1 C. This study offers an effective method for enhancing Li metal interphase stability of high‐energy‐density Li‐metal batteries.

title: Cyanoethyl Cellulose‐Mediated Polymer Electrolyte With Fast Li+ Transport and Stable Interface for Long‐Cycle Solid‑State Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
Cyano‐functionalized cellulose lowers the structural regularity of PVDF chains and introduces dynamic CN–Li+ coordination sites, thereby weakening Li+–TFSI− association and promoting salt dissociation. The resulting disordered polymer network enables faster Li+ migration, higher Li+ transference number, improved membrane robustness, and more stable electrode interfaces for durable SSLMBs.








ABSTRACT
Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are promising for solid‐state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs) owing to their safety, flexibility, and processability. However, simultaneously achieving fast Li+ transport and stable electrode/electrolyte interface remains a great challenge. Herein, a cyanoethyl cellulose (CEC)‐mediated polymer–polymer modulation strategy is proposed to construct high‐performance Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)/lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) composite electrolyte (PL‐CEC). Functional CEC effectively disrupts the ordered stacking structure of PVDF chains, while abundant polar cyano groups in CEC precisely modulate the local Li+ coordination environment, promote Li salt dissociation and fast Li+ migration. The optimized PL‐CEC exhibits high room‐temperature ionic conductivity and superior Li+ transference number. Moreover, PL‐CEC stabilizes both electrode interfaces, suppressing Li dendrite growth and high‐voltage electrolyte decomposition. Consequently, Li|PL‐CEC|Li cells realize stable Li plating/stripping for 1400 h at 0.4 mA cm−2 and 0.4 mAh cm−2. Li|PL‐CEC|LiFePO4 full cells retain 74.2% capacity after 5000 cycles at 2 C and Li|PL‐CEC|LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cells deliver excellent cycling durability and high‐rate capability. Notably, multilayer Li|PL‐CEC|NCM811 pouch cell achieves Ah‐level capacity, demonstrating the practical scalability of PL‐CEC. This work establishes a molecular‐chain engineering strategy to enhance Li+ transport and electrode interfacial stability for advanced SPEs toward long‐cycle SSLMBs.

title: Unlocking Fast and Durable Li+ Transport Beyond Polymer Segmental Dynamics for High‐Rate and Long‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
A dynamic coordination network reconstructs Li+ transport beyond polymer segmental dynamics, enabling continuous low‐energy‐barrier ion hopping in a microphase‐separated polymer electrolyte. The resulting electrolyte simultaneously delivers ultrafast charging, ultralong cycling stability, and exceptional thermal robustness for lithium metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Polymer electrolytes are promising for safe lithium metal batteries, yet their ionic transport is fundamentally limited by polymer segmental dynamics, hindering fast charging and long‐term cycling. Here, we report a microphase‐separated quasi‐solid‐state polymer electrolyte that enables rapid and durable Li+ transport through localized coordination regulation. Covalently tethered pyrrolidinium ionic liquid moieties promote lithium salt dissociation while suppressing anion migration, whereas in situ generated thioether linkages weaken Li+‐polymer interactions and enhance chain flexibility. Their synergistic integration creates a dynamic coordination environment that facilitates low‐energy Li+ hopping between adjacent coordination sites, substantially reduced ion transport dependence on polymer segmental dynamics. As a result, the optimized electrolyte delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 1.13 mS cm−1, a high Li+ transference number of 0.82, and a low activation energy of 0.17 eV. The accelerated and homogeneous Li+ transport promotes stable lithium deposition, enabling lithium metal batteries with 97.9% capacity retention after 2500 cycles at 10C and stable operation for 400 cycles at 5C even at 120°C. More broadly, this work demonstrates a viable pathway to break the conventional trade‐off between polymer processability and ion‐transport kinetics, offering a new paradigm for high‐performance solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Dissociation‐Migration Trade‐Off in Gel Polymer Electrolytes Enables Extreme‐Condition Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
Molecular regulation by the polymer matrix balances salt dissociation and Li+ migration in gel polymer electrolytes. Intermediate polymer–Li+ interactions promote Li+ transport, suppress electrolyte decomposition, and enable homogeneous interphase formation. This molecular balance enables lithium metal batteries to operate across wide temperatures, high voltages, and rates, and in practical pouch cells.








ABSTRACT
Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) under extreme conditions due to their relatively high ionic conductivity, enhanced safety, and intimate electrode contact. Despite these advantages, how polymer chemistry governs Li+ transport and interfacial reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a dissociation‐migration trade‐off principle using GPEs incorporating polymer motifs with distinct Li+ affinities, revealing that intermediate polymer–Li+ interactions balance carrier generation with Li+ migration. The optimized GPE achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.78 mS cm−1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.88 at 30°C, while suppressing excessive electrolyte decomposition and promoting stable electrode–electrolyte interphases with reduced organic accumulation and more uniform depth distributions of inorganic components. Consequently, Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cells operate across extreme conditions including −40–80°C, 4.6 V, and 4 C, retaining 80.8% capacity after 1100 cycles at −20°C. Furthermore, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers 342.7 Wh kg−1 and retains 80.3% capacity after 200 cycles. This work provides a molecular framework for the rational design of GPEs that integrate efficient ion transport with interfacial stability.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
content:
The search for sustainable indoor photovoltaics (IPVs) extends beyond conventional absorbers toward potentially cheaper, safer, and more stable alternatives. This review explores Se, Sb2S3, Sb2(S,Se)3, GeS, and Cu2ZnSnS4, Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 as potential dark‐horse candidates for future IPVs, examining their material properties, device engineering, stability, and sustainability to identify pathways toward practical indoor energy harvesting for IoT devices and other low‐power electronics.








ABSTRACT
Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb2S3, Sb2(S,Se)3, GeS, Cu2ZnSnS4 and Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
content:
This review examines single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts for N2 conversion to ammonia and urea. Their catalytic behavior is analyzed in detail through dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. This study reveals how interactions between dual active sites influence N2 activation, intermediate conversion, and product formation, providing a mechanistic basis for high‐performance catalyst design.








ABSTRACT
N2 conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N2 adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N2 conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N2 activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N2 conversion.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
content:
Silicon anodes, widely used in liquid electrolytes, remain incompatible with solid electrolytes due to the formation of unstable solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI). Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based interface offers spatially decoupled ion‐sieving and electron‐conducting, enabling ultralow (5%) volume expansion and stable cycling. Distinct planar‐confined (2D) vs. bulk‐permeated (3D) SEI evolution pathways are revealed in solid and liquid electrolytes.








ABSTRACT
Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li+‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li+ flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
content:
Low‐temperature pretreatment preconditions amorphous Sb2Se3 precursors, regulating structural rearrangement, progressive stress relaxation, and oriented crystal reconstruction during subsequent annealing. Coupled with local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, this process promotes grain growth and preferential orientation, reduces structural disorder and defect‐related nonradiative recombination, and improves carrier transport, enabling a photovoltaic efficiency of 9.78%.








ABSTRACT
Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb2Se3). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb2Se3 chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb2Se3 absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb2Se3 films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: Electron Bridge Effect Enhanced Tandem Catalysis for Efficient Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
content:
The electronic bridge‐enhanced tandem catalytic mechanism of MoCoB has achieved efficient NO3RR, in which Mo site adsorb and activate NO3− and Co site dissociate H2O to generate Hads, while B site act as an electron bridge boosting electron and proton transfer. Moreover, the MoCoB‐based Zn‐NO3−/ethanol hybrid battery realized synchronous nitrogen oxide pollutant utilization, high‐value chemical synthesis and energy supply.








ABSTRACT
Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for wastewater remediation and ammonia (NH3) synthesis under mild conditions. However, the activity of NO3RR is hindered by the high activation barrier of nitrate (NO3−), as well as the low generation efficiency and restricted migration of active hydrogen (Hads). The development of electrocatalysts that combine efficient synergistic active sites, rapid electron transfer, and unimpeded Hads migration pathways is crucial for enhancing NO3RR performance. Here, we report a molten salt etching strategy to successfully prepare a ternary metal boride MoCoB electrocatalyst. In this catalyst, Mo site can efficiently adsorb and activate NO3−, while Co site is responsible for H2O dissociation and Hads supply. Meanwhile, B site builds an electronic bridge to enhance the electron transfer and proton migration between Mo and Co sites. Benefiting from the synergistic mechanism of electron bridge effect‐enhanced tandem catalysis, MoCoB achieves an NH3 yield rate of 61.89 mg h−1 mgcat−1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 98.73%. Furthermore, a Zn‐NO3−/ethanol hybrid battery assembled with MoCoB cathode demonstrates high power density and durable long‐term cycling stability, and the production of high‐value ammonium acetate. This work provides guidance for designing efficient NO3RR electrocatalysts and offers insights into reversible zinc‐based battery.

title: Halide‐Based Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors Deliver High‐Rate and Long‐Life All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
content:
We developed a mechanically flexible, mixed ionic‐electronic conducting oxyhalide additive, C5.5Mo, that improves cathode–electrolyte contact, facilitates local charge transport, and mitigates interfacial polarization. By reducing electrode porosity and enhancing interfacial stability, this strategy achieves 85.84% capacity retention after 20 000 cycles at 6 C, offering a promising approach for high‐rate, long‐life all‐solid‐state lithium batteries.








ABSTRACT
Interfacial side reactions and degradation of solid–solid contact limit the rate capability and cycling stability of composite cathodes in all‐solid‐state lithium batteries. Here, we introduce C5.5Mo (LiMo2O2.75Cl5.5), a functional halide oxide additive designed to maintain solid–solid contact, improve charge transport, and regulate the composite‐cathode interface. Its mixed ionic‐electronic conductivity and low Young's modulus promote a dense cathode microstructure and stable interparticle contact during cycling. Bias‐dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of composite‐cathode symmetric cells reveals lower interfacial resistance and reduced bias sensitivity, suggesting partial alleviation of space‐charge‐layer‐related transport limitations. The full‐cell system still provides a specific capacity of approximately 100 mAh g−1 at 6 C and maintains stable cycling for 20 000 cycles (capacity retention of 85.84%). This work establishes a practical additive strategy for constructing high‐rate and long‐life composite cathodes.

title: Micro 3D Printing of Silica Aerogels via Bath‐Mediated In Situ Sol–Gel Reaction
content:
Bath‐mediated in situ sol‐gel printing enables high‐resolution micro 3D printing of silica aerogels. The pH‐triggered gelation of a pre‐hydrolyzed TEOS ink forms stable silica gel filaments in the basic bath. This process yields sub‐10 µm aerogel architectures that retain nanoporous structure, high specific surface area, and low thermal conductivity for localized thermal insulation on microscale heater platforms.








ABSTRACT
Silica aerogels are attractive thermally insulating materials owing to their extremely low density and nanoporous silica networks, but their integration into miniaturized devices for thermal management remains limited by the difficulty of patterning fragile aerogel structures at microscale resolution. Here, we report a bath‐mediated in situ sol–gel reaction printing process for microscale 3D printing of silica aerogel architectures. In this strategy, a pre‐hydrolyzed, silanol‐rich precursor solution stabilized in an acidic medium is deposited into a basic bath, where an abrupt pH change triggers instantaneous siloxane condensation and forms silica gel filaments. This pH‐mediated sol–gel printing process enabled the fabrication of silica aerogel structures with filament linewidths as small as 8 µm in single‐layer patterns and approximately 20 µm in multilayer 3D structures. The printed filaments exhibited an interconnected nanoparticle network with a high specific surface area of 988.3 m2 g−1, an average pore size of 18.4 nm, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.023 W m−1 K−1. On microheater device platforms, the printed aerogels provided localized thermal insulation that could be modulated by adjusting the printed architecture. This work provides a route for integrating nanoporous silica aerogels as spatially controlled thermal insulation components in miniaturized thermal management systems.

title: Chloride‐Induced Microstructure–Covalency Coupling Enables Ultrafine Nanoparticle Exsolution for High‐Performance CO2 Electrolysis
content:
Chloride incorporation provides a dual route for controlling perovskite catalysts by reshaping the grain‐boundary (GB) network and weakening metal–oxygen bonding. This coupled structural and electronic regulation drives highly dense exsolution of ultrafine FeNi nanoparticles (NPs), creating abundant and durable active interfaces that accelerate carbon dioxide electrolysis and sustain high‐performance operation in solid oxide electrolysis cells.








ABSTRACT
Efficient CO2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires active cathode catalysts that combine abundant active interfaces, rapid charge transfer, and long‐term structural stability. Perovskite exsolution can generate robust metal nanoparticles (NPs), but achieving a dense population of ultrafine nanocatalysts remains challenging. Here, we report a chloride‐assisted exsolution strategy in Sr2Fe1.3Ni0.2Mo0.5O6‐δ (SFNM)‐based cathodes, demonstrating for the first time that Cl doping links grain‐boundary (GB) engineering with metal–oxygen covalency regulation to direct FeNi NP exsolution. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis shows that the SrCl2‐derived molten‐salt flux effect creates a faceted, GB‐rich perovskite morphology, increasing the GB density by approximately 78.9% and providing abundant nucleation sites for exsolution. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and theoretical calculations further reveal that Cl substitution attenuates metal–oxygen hybridization, promotes oxygen‐vacancy formation, and facilitates outward segregation of Fe and Ni. This chloride‐triggered dual regulation yields a highly populated FeNi NP surface, accelerating CO2 electroreduction and lowering polarization resistance. Consequently, the reduced Cl‐doped SFNM cathode (R‐SFNMCl2) achieves 2.73 A cm−2 at 800°C and 1.5 V, while sustaining stable operation for 400 h with only minor degradation. This work establishes a new halogen‐mediated exsolution design paradigm for developing high‐performance SOEC cathode catalysts.
